cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message "rootNode must not be null"
cases.description: When the supplied JsonNode is null the method should reject the call and throw an IllegalArgumentException before invoking any customizer.
If the consumer is null the method should behave as if an empty customizer was supplied; the schema (a simple schema requiring a string property "name") validates the provided node successfully.
A customizer that disables fail‑fast mode should not affect a valid instance; the validator runs to completion and returns an empty message set.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> containing exactly one message about missing required property "name"
cases.description: When fail‑fast is enabled the validator should stop after the first error; the missing required property produces a single ValidationMessage.
If the consumer throws an exception the method must propagate it unchanged; no validation should be performed.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> containing at least two messages: one for missing required property "name" and one for violating the "minimum" constraint on "age"
cases.description: A node that violates two independent schema rules triggers two separate branches inside the validator (required‑property check and numeric‑range check). Both messages must be present in the result set.

group: Schema with recursive anchor – branch exercised

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> that is empty (recursive anchor resolves without infinite loop)
cases.description: When the schema declares a recursive anchor, the validator must take the `isRecursiveAnchor()` branch; the test verifies that recursion is handled correctly and no stack overflow occurs.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> that is empty (validation succeeds even when fail‑fast is enabled because no error is produced)
cases.description: The consumer forces fail‑fast mode on the ExecutionContext. The supplied JSON instance satisfies the schema, so the validator should finish without emitting any messages. This case verifies that enabling fail‑fast does not cause a false‑positive failure.

input.value: ctx -> ctx.setMessageSource(new MessageSource() { public String getMessage(String key, Object... args) { return "[FR] " + key; } })

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> containing at least two messages whose text starts with "[FR] " (e.g., "[FR] required.property" and "[FR] numeric.minimum")
cases.description: A custom MessageSource that prefixes every message with "[FR] " is injected via the consumer. The instance violates two constraints (missing required property "name" and "age" below the minimum). The test confirms that the validator uses the supplied MessageSource for all generated messages.

cases.expected: Set<ValidationMessage> containing a message whose instanceLocation is "/address/zip" (JSON‑Pointer notation) rather than the default JSON‑Path notation (e.g., "$.address.zip")
cases.description: The consumer changes the path representation used in validation messages to JSON‑Pointer. The schema requires "zip" to match a numeric pattern, so the provided string is invalid. The test checks that the instanceLocation in the resulting ValidationMessage follows the JSON‑Pointer format, proving that the customizer correctly influences the ExecutionContext.
